p: St James Quarter sits right where the New Town meets the busier east end of the city, and it's a cracking launch pad. Arriving from the airport? The tram runs all the way to Picardy Place, just on the doorstep, so you can drop your bags and be browsing within minutes.

Across the road, Edinburgh Playhouse is one of the biggest theatres in the country for touring musicals, so a shopping afternoon followed by an evening show is an easy combination. On Queen Street, the Scottish National Portrait Gallery is a stunning red sandstone building full of faces from Scottish history, and its grand entrance hall alone is worth a look.

Calton Hill, as mentioned, is only a few minutes away and gives you one of the best views over the city, including Arthur's Seat, the Firth of Forth and down Princes Street towards the castle. Head south over the bridges near Waverley and you'll be on the Royal Mile in no time, with Holyrood Palace at its foot.

Timing makes a big difference in Edinburgh. In August, when the festivals take over, the city is buzzing but heaving, so expect queues for food and plan any bookings early. A visit on a quieter weekday morning is far more relaxed if you just fancy an easy browse and lunch.
For families, it's a dependable indoor base with toilets, food and space to regroup between sightseeing, which is worth a lot on a long day in a busy capital city.
